column2: The deep blue forest had not changed at all, yet to the grown-up Cecia it felt far more precious than before.
The forest embraced and protected everything, but she knew that even this world of the forest would not last forever.
One day the forest would be joined to the world outside, and no one could live in it alone.

Whenever the children of the forest begged for stories of the outside world, she told them vividly what it was like: stone buildings taller than trees, markets crowded with more people than you could count, food no one had ever seen.
And at the end she always told them that the people outside were no different from them, people who loved peace and their families just the same.
The little children always listened with shining eyes.
Cecia never stopped praying that when the children one day widened their world, their future would be peaceful and rich.
To the people and the world I love, all my tenderness, forever...
Satan's dragon was gone, and peace had returned to Arcaya, the world below...
It feels as if a long time has passed since I left their land...
In a world still scarred by the dragon's claws and the chaos, they each took a new step forward.
Cecia went back to the Forest of Reyforia. With St. Diana's return, the forest was overjoyed.
For a while, I imagine, her days were spent making reports to the elders and talking with everyone who came to visit Cecia.

Then, when the excitement faded and she was alone, she seems to have gone to the Forest of the Holy Mother to think about what lay ahead. Lost quietly in thought, perhaps she can see the forest of the future.
I will keep praying that when the forest one day mingles with the outside world... it will be a wonderful thing for the forest and for her...
Again and again I recall the days I spent with them, and the memories shine.
I am grateful from the bottom of my heart that I met them.
O small star of the great light... May tenderness and great blessings be upon everyone who lives there, upon all of the world I love...
Back from her journey, Cecia did not return to the forest of her homeland but to the Forest of the Holy Mother.
She seemed to feel that something of hers still remained there.
It was a lonely life, but protecting the forest meant more to her than anything.
Like many Holy Mothers before her, she lived there until she grew old,
praying for the peace of the world.
Her prayers embraced the world, forever and ever...
Clive Saingrent: the days of fighting his own blood were over, and peace came to his heart.
From a life wandering through cold nights to a world bathed in warm sunlight. The breath of life in all its forms, unlike anything he had felt before, enfolded him anew.
Now that the world and he himself were as they should be, he looked for a new path to live by.
He chose to hone his swordsmanship, and lived as a mercenary knight, fighting for what he believed in.
The life of travelling the world with his comrades became the best days of his life.
The years went by, and for his deeds he became lord of a small country. In that small, peaceful land he was loved by the people as a ruler of heart and courage.
What he had sought, and what had been sought of him, he found, and he lived out his life to the full.
Clive seems to have shaken off the temptation of blood and to be trying to live in the sunlight.
Through the journey to save the world he must have looked hard at himself, and thought long about what it means to live cursing yourself.
